# Native replay

<!-- Generated by scripts/run_native_replay.py; do not edit by hand. -->

Each concrete input runs on the native function (Python, Go, Rust, TypeScript, Solidity) through
a driver in `proofs/replay/` and on a `.mm` port pinned to that input. See
[RESULTS.md](RESULTS.md) for the contract benchmark itself.

## Reference ports

71 of 71 inputs (71 cases) give the
same verdict natively and on the hand-written ports, for both the buggy and the fixed version.


## LLM witnesses (LLM only arm)

Every "violated" verdict's witness is parsed as `name = value` pairs for the port's parameters
and replayed on the native code. Free text is never executed; a witness without a value for
every parameter, or one that needs an oversized collection, is unexpressible.

| version | reproduced | not reproduced | unexpressible |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| buggy | 174 | 0 | 38 |
| fixed | 1 | 2 | 11 |

Witnesses against the fixed version:

- GO01-D05 (run 1): unexpressible — no value for locations
- GO01-D05 (run 2): unexpressible — no value for locations
- GO01-D05 (run 3): unexpressible — no value for locations
- GO02-D03 (run 2): not reproduced — run -top -1 -> -top must not be negative
- GO02-D03 (run 3): not reproduced — run -top -1 -> -top must not be negative
- GO03-D06 (run 1): reproduced — rotate -> 204, 0 sessions left, epoch -9223372036854775808
- GO03-D07 (run 1): unexpressible — no value for password_matches
- PY02-D04 (run 1): unexpressible — no value for row, n
- PY02-D04 (run 2): unexpressible — row: '"worker"' is not an integer
- PY02-D04 (run 3): unexpressible — row: '"worker"' is not an integer
- RS03-D08 (run 1): unexpressible — rows = 9223372036854775807 needs a collection larger than 100000
- RS03-D08 (run 3): unexpressible — cols = 9223372036854775807 needs a collection larger than 100000
- TS01-D12 (run 2): unexpressible — n = 9007199254740994 needs a collection larger than 100000
- TS01-D12 (run 3): unexpressible — n = 9007199254740994 needs a collection larger than 100000

## LLM ports (mumei + LLM arm)

Each port the LLM wrote is pinned to the case's first reference input and compared with the
native verdict on the same input. "behaviour changed" means the port no longer does what the
native code does, typically because the bug was fixed while translating.

| version | matches | behaviour changed | inconclusive | no port |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| buggy | 182 | 29 | 2 | 0 |
| fixed | 207 | 1 | 5 | 0 |

Behaviour changed in: GO01-D04 (buggy), GO02-D01 (buggy), GO02-D02 (buggy), GO02-D03 (buggy), PY02-D04 (buggy), PY02-D05 (fixed), PY03-D05 (buggy), RS03-D02 (buggy), RS03-D04 (buggy), SOL01-D03 (buggy), SOL01-D08 (buggy), TS01-D03 (buggy), TS01-D07 (buggy), TS03-D09 (buggy).
